Question:
Can you provide the highest and lowest profits for Italian customers segmented into ten evenly divided tiers based on their December 2021 sales profits?

4 candidates were produced independently. Each shows its SQL and the first rows of its result.

[A]
SQL:
WITH customer_profits AS (
  SELECT p.cust_id, SUM(p.amount_sold - p.TOTAL_COST) as total_profit
  FROM profits p
  JOIN customers c ON p.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  JOIN times t ON p.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'Italy'
    AND t.calendar_year = 2021
    AND t.calendar_month_name = 'December'
  GROUP BY p.cust_id
),
ranked_profits AS (
  SELECT 
    cust_id,
    total_profit,
    NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY total_profit) as profit_tier
  FROM customer_profits
)
SELECT 
  profit_tier,
  MIN(total_profit) as min_profit,
  MAX(total_profit) as max_profit,
  COUNT(*) as customer_count
FROM ranked_profits
GROUP BY profit_tier
ORDER BY profit_tier

  cust_id, cust_first_name, cust_last_name, total_profit, profit_tier
FROM (
  SELECT 
    c.cust_id,
    c.cust_first_name,
    c.cust_last_name,
    SUM(p.amount_sold - p.TOTAL_COST) as total_profit,
    NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY SUM(p.amount_sold - p.TOTAL_COST)) as profit_tier
  FROM profits p
  JOIN customers c ON p.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'Italy'
    AND p.time_id >= '2021-12-01' 
    AND p.time_id < '2022-01-01'
  GROUP BY c.cust_id, c.cust_first_name, c.cust_last_name
)
ORDER BY total_profit DESC
